Chapter 2: Proposed System

2.1 Scope & Objectives

The proposed IT Asset & Support Desk Management System (AssetDesk) is engineered as an integrated, secure web platform to modernize internal IT governance. The scope is purposefully defined to fulfill core enterprise IT operational requirements while maintaining simplicity, reliability, and ease of demonstration during academic review.

System Boundary & Scope Definition

In-Scope Engineering Features Out-of-Scope Elements (Deliberate Exclusions)
  • Role-Based Access Control (ADMIN, IT_SUPPORT, EMPLOYEE)
  • Hardware asset lifecycle management (CRUD, assign, unassign)
  • Software license seat allocation & key masking
  • Automated cron-based license expiry alert checks
  • Support ticketing workflow with comments & SLA calculation
  • Append-only security audit log recording system mutations
  • Executive dashboard summary cards & CSV export reports
  • Payment gateways, billing systems & e-commerce checkout
  • Native mobile apps (iOS / Android platform binaries)
  • Physical barcode/RFID scanner hardware integrations
  • Enterprise Single Sign-On (SSO / SAML / Active Directory)
  • AI automated ticket resolution bots / NLP chat agents
  • Multi-tenant multi-company database schema partitioning

Core Engineering Objectives

  1. Centralized Asset Inventory: Establish a single, auditable repository for all computing hardware with serials, specs, and status tracking.
  2. Custody & Ownership Tracking: Prevent hardware shrinkage through atomic, concurrency-safe equipment assignment to designated staff members.
  3. Software License Compliance: Enforce strict seat allocation limits and alert administrators automatically 30 days prior to license expirations.
  4. Structured Incident Resolution: Provide employees an intuitive portal to log support requests, enforcing SLA deadlines and a transparent 4-stage lifecycle.
  5. Accountability & Audit Logging: Record every administrative modification automatically in an immutable, read-only audit log.
  6. Administrative Intelligence: Deliver operational visibility via real-time dashboard KPIs and downloadable CSV reports for management.

2.2 Advantages of Proposed System

The proposed web platform eliminates the inherent vulnerabilities of manual spreadsheet records, email-based helpdesk queues, and untracked asset handovers. Table 2.1 details the comparative advantages achieved across each architectural module:

Table 2.1: Operational Advantages of the Proposed System
Advantage Technical & Operational Explanation Module
Centralized Record Replaces scattered desktop spreadsheets with a single, indexed database accessible via secure API endpoints. M2, M3
Role-Based Access Enforces strict privilege boundaries so employees only access their assigned items, while administrators manage configuration. M1
Immutable Audit Trail Every status change, assignment, and profile modification is captured permanently with timestamp, user ID, and IP address. M5
Seat Quota Control Prevents vendor compliance violations by restricting license allocations to purchased seat thresholds using atomic validation. M3
Proactive Expiry Alerts Automated daily cron jobs detect licenses nearing expiration (≤30 days) and highlight them prominently on the dashboard. M3, M5
SLA Ticket Tracking Computes deterministic resolution deadlines based on ticket priority (High: 8h, Medium: 24h, Low: 72h) to eliminate forgotten tasks. M4
Exportable CSV Reports Enables one-click generation of formatted CSV files for physical audits, accounting reconciliations, and executive meetings. M5
Universal Web Access Runs seamlessly across desktop and mobile browsers via a responsive React SPA without requiring local client installations. All Modules
Operational Impact: Transitioning from unstructured email chains to AssetDesk reduces asset retrieval ambiguity to zero and guarantees an unbroken chain of custody for all corporate equipment.

2.3 Feasibility Study

Prior to full-scale development, a rigorous three-pillar feasibility evaluation was conducted to confirm the technical, economical, and operational viability of the project within institutional constraints.

2.3.1 Technical Feasibility

The selected technology stack—Node.js, Express, React, Vite, and MongoDB—represents widely adopted, mature, and extensively documented industry standards. JavaScript is utilized across both client and server tiers, eliminating context switching and serialization overhead. The candidate possessed foundational coursework in database modeling and web frameworks, ensuring all technical requirements (REST APIs, JWT encryption, state machines) were fully realizable within standard engineering capabilities.

2.3.2 Economical Feasibility

The project incurs zero software licensing or subscription expenditure. All runtime frameworks, compilers, libraries, and IDE tools are distributed under permissive open-source licenses (MIT/Apache 2.0). Deployment utilizes generous free-tier cloud hosting (Render for API, Vercel for SPA, and MongoDB Atlas for database clusters). No proprietary hardware or specialized servers were required.

Component / Resource Tool / Cloud Provider Licensing & Cost
Runtime & Web Framework Node.js 20 LTS & Express 4.21 Free / Open-Source (MIT)
Frontend SPA & Tooling React 18.3 & Vite 5.4 Free / Open-Source (MIT)
Database Cluster MongoDB 7 / MongoDB Atlas Cloud Free Tier (M0 Sandbox)
Application Hosting Render Web Service & Vercel Edge Free Tier (Community)
Development & Testing VS Code, Git, Jest, Playwright Free / Open-Source

2.3.3 Operational Feasibility

The user interface follows clean, responsive, and intuitive web design principles. Standard HTML forms, clear status badges, and descriptive confirmation dialogs ensure that minimal onboarding or training is required for end users. The role-tailored navigation dynamically presents only the actions appropriate to the authenticated user's permission level.
